Below is a consolidated, coach-ready 12‑week program you can hand to your client (start date: 2026‑06‑01). It integrates heavy resistance for bone and strength, hypertrophy and single‑leg work, a progressive periodization with de‑loads, cardio for aerobic fitness, a nutrition plan tailored to perimenopause and bone health, cooling and vasomotor‑sensitive measures, and safe 1RM testing at the end. Hot yoga and fasted HIIT were excluded for safety; cooler yoga/mobility alternatives are included. Phase 2 intensity was pushed as requested.

Summary overview
- Client: 47 F, advanced lifter, early perimenopause (cycle 23–52 d), significant vasomotor symptoms (hot flashes, heat intolerance). GP cleared for full resistance training including bone loading. Restrictions: no sauna, no fasted HIIT in heat. All sessions to occur in cool/AC environment where possible; structured cooling used pre/during/post.
- Frequency: 4 resistance sessions/wk + 2 cool mobility/yoga sessions/wk + 2–3 cardio sessions/wk (90–150 min cardio/week). One full rest day/week.
- Periodization: 3 phases, each 4 weeks: Phase 1 Foundation (Weeks 1–4), Phase 2 Build & intensity (Weeks 5–8, pushed intensity), Phase 3 Strength & testing (Weeks 9–12). Weeks 4, 8, 12 are de-load/recovery focus weeks.
- Strength priority maintained: 2 heavy strength days (lower/upper) + 2 hypertrophy/assistance days per week. Cardio scheduled to avoid interference with heavy days when possible.
- Nutrition: targets for protein (1.6–2.2 g/kg), calcium/vitamin D emphasis, creatine recommended, pre/post training carbohydrate timing, hydration & electrolytes, and strategies to limit vasomotor triggers.
- Safety: long rests on heavy sets, cooling between sets (fan, cold towel to neck/face, chilled drinks), pre-feed for interval/high-intensity work, monitoring of hot flashes and symptoms, abort criteria, and informed consent for 1RM testing. No hot yoga or fasted HIIT.

Phase-by-phase structure (detailed weekly plan)

Phase 1 — Foundation & acclimation (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: re-establish heavy baseline, technique, establish cooling routines and cardio base.

Week 1 (2026-06-01 → 06-07)
- Day 1 — Strength Lower (Squat focus)
  - Warm-up + pre-cool (cold drink, towel)
  - Back squat: 5 × 5 @ ~75% 1RM, 3–4 min rests
  - Romanian DL: 3 × 6 @ RPE 7
  - DB split squat: 3 × 8/leg
  - Farmer carries: 3 × 40–60 m
  - Mobility + post-session cooling

- Day 2 — Strength Upper (Push/Pull)
  - Bench/incline: 5 × 5 @ ~75% 1RM
  - Bent-over or single-arm row: 4 × 6–8
  - OHP: 3 × 6
  - Face pulls: 3 × 12
  - Core planks: 3 × 40–60 s
  - Cooling between sets

- Day 3 — Active recovery
  - Pool walking or brisk walk 20–30 min in cool environment
  - Breathing practice and relaxation

- Day 4 — Hypertrophy Lower (posterior focus)
  - Deadlift: 4 × 6 @ ~70% 1RM
  - G‑Ham raise or Nordic: 3 × 6–8
  - Bulgarian split squat: 3 × 10/leg
  - Band hip abduction: 3 × 15
  - Cool-down + cooling

- Day 5 — Hypertrophy Upper
  - Incline DB press: 4 × 8–10
  - Pull-ups/lat pulldown: 4 × 6–8
  - Single-arm DB row: 3 × 10/arm
  - Lateral raises: 3 × 12–15
  - Core anti-rotation: 3 × 8–10/side

- Days 6–7 — Rest / low activity (short cool walks, sleep hygiene)

Cardio Week 1
- Cardio A: LISS 30–35 min (walk/bike in cool)
- Cardio B: Pool 20–30 min
- Optional Cardio C: 20–30 min easy walk

Week 2 (06-08 → 06-14)
- Progress: increase main-lift load 2–3.5% if RPE low; same structure as Week 1.
- Cardio: LISS 35–40 min; short interval session in cool environment (6 × 1 min hard with 2 min easy) — fed before intervals; pool session as recovery.

Week 3 (06-15 → 06-21)
- Intensify slightly
  - Strength days move to heavier sets: e.g., 5 × 3 @ 82–85% 1RM for main lifts; accessory volume slightly reduced.
- Cardio: intervals 8 × 45–60 s (AC bike/rower) + LISS and pool.

Week 4 — De-load (06-22 → 06-28)
- Reduce intensity/volume by ~40–50%: main lifts 60–65% 1RM × 3–4 sets × 5–6 reps or RPE 6; accessory volume halved.
- Cardio limited to low-intensity pool/walks (no intervals).
- Focus on sleep, hydration, nutrition and symptom tracking.

Phase 2 — Build & higher intensity (Weeks 5–8) — PUSHED INTENSITY
Goals: raise main lift intensity, heavier accessories, added low-volume power/plyo for bone stimulus, more aggressive cardio intervals (in cool setting), but keep strict cooling and recovery.

Week 5 (06-29 → 07-05)
- Day 1 — Strength Lower (Heavy + power)
  - Back squat: 6 × 3 @ ~85% 1RM
  - Paused squat: 3 × 2 @ 70–75%
  - Trap-bar deadlift: 4 × 4 @ ~80%
  - Box jumps (low): 4 × 3
  - Heavy carries: 4 × 40–60 m

- Day 2 — Strength Upper (Push emphasis)
  - Bench press: 6 × 3 @ ~85% 1RM
  - Incline/close-grip bench: 4 × 4–6
  - Weighted chin-ups: 4 × 4–6
  - OHP: 3 × 5
  - Heavy loaded carries

- Day 3 — Active recovery: Pool 25–35 min + mobility

- Day 4 — Hypertrophy Lower
  - Deadlift (conventional): 5 × 3 @ ~85%
  - RDL: 3 × 6 heavy
  - Bulgarian split squat: 4 × 6–8 heavy
  - G‑Ham: 3 × 6–8

- Day 5 — Hypertrophy Upper
  - OHP: 4 × 4–6
  - Heavy row: 4 × 5
  - Incline DB press: 3 × 6–8
  - Face pulls + rotator cuff work

- Pool recovery 25–35 min.
- LISS 30–40 min walk or bike.

Week 6 (07-06 → 07-12)
- Day 1 — Strength Lower
  - Squat: 5 × 2 at ~88–90% (heavy doubles)
  - Pause squats: 3 × 2 at 75%
  - DL variant: 4 × 3 @ 85%
  - Sled pushes/prowler: 6 × 20–30 m
  - Carries

- Day 2 — Strength Upper
  - Bench: 5 × 2 @ 88–90% (heavy doubles/triples)

  - Weighted pull-ups: 4 × 4–6

- Day 3 — Pool 20–30 min + mobility

  - G‑Ham: 3 × 6–8
  - Low-vol plyo: 4 × 3

- Day 5 — Hypertrophy Upper
  - OHP 4 × 4
  - Rows 4 × 5
  - Incline DB 3 × 6
  - Superset accessories

Cardio Week 6

- LISS 40–45 min.
- Pool recovery 20–30 min.

Week 7 (07-13 → 07-19) — Peak intensity
- Day 1 — Strength Lower (peak)
  - Squat: work up to heavy single/double at RPE 9–9.5 (e.g., 92–94% or top singles per athlete), 4–6 top sets with full rest
  - Minimal accessory volume

- Day 2 — Strength Upper (peak)
  - Bench: work up to heavy single/double at RPE 9–9.5
  - Minimal accessory volume

- Day 3 — Pool recovery + mobility

- Day 4 — Hypertrophy Lower (reduced volume)
  - DL: 3 × 2–3 @ 87–90%
  - Bulgarian/step-up: 3 × 6
  - G‑Ham: 3 × 6

- Day 5 — Hypertrophy Upper (reduced volume)
  - OHP: 3 × 4
  - Row: 3 × 5
  - Incline DB: 3 × 6–8

Cardio Week 7
- Short high-quality interval (AC): 8 × 45–60 s RPE 8–9
- LISS 30–40 min or pool 30 min
- Optional light recovery walk

Week 8 — De-load (07-20 → 07-26)
- Reduce intensity/volume 40–60%. Main lifts at ~60–70% 1RM with fewer sets.
- Cardio limited to pool/walks; no intervals this week.
- Focus on sleep, nutrition, hydration, symptoms.

Phase 3 — Strength refinement & testing (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: convert build into high-quality strength, retain hypertrophy, finalize 1RM testing protocol (safe testing in Week 11–12), and deload after testing.

Week 9 (07-27 → 08-02)
- Day 1 — Strength Lower
  - Back squat: 5 × 3 @ ~85% 1RM
  - Single-leg accessory: 3 × 6–8/leg
  - Carries and mobility

- Day 2 — Strength Upper
  - Bench: 5 × 3 @ ~85%
  - Heavy rows and OHP: 3 × 5

- Day 3 — Recovery: pool 20–30 min + breathing work

- Day 4 — Hypertrophy Lower
  - Deadlift: 4 × 4 @ 80%
  - Low plyo: 3 × 3
  - Accessory posterior chain work

- Day 5 — Hypertrophy Upper
  - 4 × 6–8 pressing and pulling, accessory and rotator cuff

Cardio Week 9

- LISS 35–45 min.
- Pool 20–30 min.

Week 10 (08-03 → 08-09)
- Increase intensity slightly
  - Squat/Bench: doubles at 87–90% (work sets)
  - Deadlift 4 × 3 @ 82–85%

  - Bench press: 6 × 3 @ ~85% 1RM

  - Weighted chin-ups: 4 × 4–6

  - Heavy loaded carries

- Day 4 — Hypertrophy Lower
  - Deadlift (conventional): 5 × 3 @ ~85%
  - RDL: 3 × 6 heavy
  - Bulgarian split squat: 4 × 6–8 heavy
  - G‑Ham: 3 × 6–8

- Day 5 — Hypertrophy Upper
  - OHP: 4 × 4–6
  - Heavy row: 4 × 5

  - Face pulls + rotator cuff work

- Interval (AC bike/rower) 8 × 1 min hard w/90–120 s recoveries (pre-feed 20–30 g carbs).
- Pool recovery 25–35 min.
- LISS 30–40 min walk or bike.

- Day 1 — Strength Lower
  - Squat: 5 × 2 at ~88–90% (heavy doubles)
  - Pause squats: 3 × 2 at 75%
  - DL variant: 4 × 3 @ 85%
  - Sled pushes/prowler: 6 × 20–30 m
  - Carries

- Day 2 — Strength Upper
  - Bench: 5 × 2 @ 88–90% (heavy doubles/triples)
  - Close-grip bench: 4 × 4–6
  - Weighted pull-ups: 4 × 4–6
  - OHP: 3 × 4–5

- Day 3 — Pool 20–30 min + mobility

- Day 4 — Hypertrophy Lower
  - Deadlift: 4 × 3 @ ~87–88%
  - Bulgarian split: 4 × 6 heavy
  - G‑Ham: 3 × 6–8
  - Low-vol plyo: 4 × 3

- Day 5 — Hypertrophy Upper
  - OHP 4 × 4
  - Rows 4 × 5
  - Incline DB 3 × 6
  - Superset accessories

- Interval (AC) 10 × 1 min hard w/90–120 s recoveries (pre-feed).
- LISS 40–45 min.

- Day 1 — Strength Lower (peak)
  - Squat: work up to heavy single/double at RPE 9–9.5 (e.g., 92–94% or top singles per athlete), 4–6 top sets with full rest
  - Minimal accessory volume

  - Bench: work up to heavy single/double at RPE 9–9.5
  - Minimal accessory volume

- Day 3 — Pool recovery + mobility

  - Bulgarian/step-up: 3 × 6

Goals: convert build into high-quality strength, retain hypertrophy, finalize 1RM testing protocol (safe testing in Week 11–12), and deload after testing.

- Day 1 — Strength Lower
  - Back squat: 5 × 3 @ ~85% 1RM
  - Single-leg accessory: 3 × 6–8/leg
  - Carries and mobility

- Day 2 — Strength Upper
  - Bench: 5 × 3 @ ~85%
  - Heavy rows and OHP: 3 × 5

- Day 3 — Recovery: pool 20–30 min + breathing work

- Day 4 — Hypertrophy Lower
  - Deadlift: 4 × 4 @ 80%
  - Low plyo: 3 × 3
  - Accessory posterior chain work

- Day 5 — Hypertrophy Upper
  - 4 × 6–8 pressing and pulling, accessory and rotator cuff

- LISS 35–45 min.
- Pool 20–30 min.

- Increase intensity slightly
  - Squat/Bench: doubles at 87–90% (work sets)
  - Deadlift 4 × 3 @ 82–85%
  - Accessory volume kept moderate

Cardio Week 10
- Interval session: 5 × 3 min at RPE 6.5–7.5 w/3 min recovery (AC)
- Long LISS 40–45 min
- Pool recovery

Week 11 (08-10 → 08-16) — Peak before testing
- Early week: taper slightly; keep intensity high but reduce volume to prime for testing.
- Testing option: perform 1RM test for selected lifts in a cool environment using conservative ramp (see Testing Protocol below). Consider splitting testing across two days: Squat + Bench Day A; Deadlift Day B (48–72 h apart) for safety and recovery.
- If testing: prioritize cooling, long rests, spotters, pre-feed, and stop criteria.

Week 12 (08-17 → 08-23) — De-load & recovery post-test
- If testing done in Week 11, Week 12 is a recovery/de-load week: low volume, moderate loads 50–70% 1RM, minimal accessory work, pool sessions and mobility.
- If testing performed early Week 12, keep remaining days for recovery and avoid heat/saunas.

1RM Testing protocol (recommended)
- Environment: Cool AC room, fans, cold towels, chilled drink, experienced spotters, 4–6 min rest between top attempts.
- Warm-up ramp example (squat):
  - Empty bar × 8–10; 40% × 5; 60% × 3; 75% × 2; 85% × 1; 95% projected attempt → adjust by feel. Limit to 2–3 top attempts. Same for bench. Deadlift needs fewer warm sets.
- Pre-feed: 20–40 g carbs + 15–25 g protein 30–60 min pre-test. Not fasted.
- Stop criteria: dizziness, severe flushing, palpitations, near-syncope, acute pain — abort, cool and hydrate.
- Alternative: 2–3RM test and estimate 1RM to reduce risk.

Mobility / Yoga (cool environment) — twice weekly
- Replace hot yoga with cool-room yoga or mobility sessions twice per week (25–35 min), scheduled on active recovery days or after lighter sessions.
- Sessions include breath work (diaphragmatic breathing), thoracic mobility, hip flexor and glute stretches, shoulder openers, hamstring mobility and long holds, plus restorative poses for parasympathetic recovery.

Cardio plan (integrated across weeks)
- 2–3 cardio sessions weekly (mix of LISS, pool, and interval work in cool environment).
- Interval work limited to ≤12–18 minutes total high-intensity time per week; always pre-fed, done in AC or pool, and scheduled to minimize interference with heavy strength days.
- LISS (30–45 min) and pool sessions emphasize cooling and recovery and provide aerobic maintenance.

Nutrition plan summary (perimenopause & bone health)
- Calories: maintenance or slight surplus +100–250 kcal for muscle/bone; modest deficit -200–300 kcal if fat loss goal (but avoid aggressive deficits with heavy training).
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day (spread across 3–4 meals; 25–40 g per meal)
- Carbs: 2–4 g/kg/day (prioritize pre/post training carbs; small snack 20–40 g carbs + 15–25 g protein before interval/high-intensity sessions)
- Fat: 20–30% total calories with omega‑3 sources (salmon, sardines, fish oil)
- Calcium: 1,000–1,200 mg/day via diet (dairy/fortified foods) ± supplement if needed (split doses)
- Vitamin D: per GP/blood test (commonly 1,000–2,000 IU/day or higher if deficient)
- Creatine: 3–5 g/day recommended for performance and muscle support
- Magnesium: 200–400 mg at bedtime if intake low
- Avoid hot/spicy foods and hot drinks around sessions that trigger hot flashes; favor cool meals/drinks pre/post training
- Hydration & electrolytes: 2–3 L/day baseline; electrolyte drink during heavy sweating or long sessions

Cooling & vasomotor management (applies to all sessions)
- Pre-cool: 10–15 min with cool fluids, cold towel/neck wrap; consider a cooling vest if client prefers
- During sessions: fan directed at face/neck; chilled drink; cold towel between heavy sets; longer rests (3–5 min on heavy sets)
- Post-session: cool shower/ice packs to neck/upper back; 20–30 min cooling period before outdoor/hot exposure
- Avoid sauna, hot tubs, hot yoga; avoid fasted HIIT in heat
- If acute severe vasomotor symptoms during session: stop, move to cool area, cool towel/ice pack to neck, hydrate, sit/lie down; seek medical help if near-syncope or fainting occurs

Progression and autoregulation
- Increase main-lift loads 1–5 lb (0.5–2.5%) per week if last set felt ≥2 RIR. If RPE ≥9, repeat or reduce load next session.
- Use RPE, symptom log (hot flashes, sleep, energy), and performance to autoregulate. If symptoms increase, reduce intensity/volume or substitute pool/recovery sessions.

Monitoring & checkpoints
- Weekly: track training loads, RPE, hot flash frequency/severity, sleep, and hunger/mood.
- Mid-program reassessment at start of Week 5 (end of Phase 1): adjust loads, nutrition, and cardio based on response and symptom log.
- Before 1RM testing: confirm stable symptom profile over prior 7–10 days and client readiness.

Sample microcycle (example week template for heavy week)
- Mon: Strength Lower (heavy)
- Tue: Interval Cardio (AC) + cool mobility (or Strength Upper if preferred, avoid interval same day as heavy lower)
- Wed: Strength Upper (heavy) + short cool walk
- Thu: Pool mobility/yoga (cool) + light LISS
- Fri: Hypertrophy Lower (heavy accessory)
- Sat: Hypertrophy Upper + LISS 20–30 min
- Sun: Rest

Practical notes for you as trainer
- Schedule sessions in coolest gym hours; keep several fans, cold towels, chilled water, and quick access to a pool or cool room.
- Keep sessions focused, limit overall session time to ~60–75 min on heavy days including warm-up.
- Communicate frequently about hot flashes, dizziness, or abnormal symptoms; have an emergency cooling and medical plan.
- If client wants printable session cards or exact loads based on current 1RMs, provide her latest 1RMs or current training weights and I will calculate week-by-week loads and printable cards.
